# Database

## Making and Testing Schema Changes on a Local DB Instance

The database schema and migrations are managed by [golang-migrate](https://github.com/golang-migrate/migrate). Run `brew bundle` to install this tool along with other CLI tools useful for this project.

- Create new `sql` files in the `db/migrations` folder with `migrate create -ext sql -dir db/migrations <migration file name>`.
  - The file name should be `the_change.up.sql` and a `.down.sql` file should also be created for revert the migration if needed.
- Test your migrations changes by starting a local in-memory database with `make dev-start`
- Run the migration changes with `make dev-migrate-up`

## Staging - Making Schema Changes on the DB Cluster

1. Connect to the prod VPN, see setup direction [here](https://thehub.github.com/security/security-operations/production-vpn-access/)

1. Navigate to the [project's DB cluster page on the ProfessorX app](https://professorx.githubapp.com/mysql/cluster/trust-metadata-api-staging), you will find the password for user `trust_metadata_api_stag_super_0`, which we use to connect with the database on this page

> ⚠️ Only use the super user for running migrations. All other access to the database should use the `vt_app_devel` user and vitess gateway `vitess-vtgate-mysql-staging.service.iad.github.net` which you can find on the [ProfessorX page](https://professorx.githubapp.com/mysql/cluster/trust-metadata-api-staging)

1. Connect to the cluster with

```shell
mysql -u trust_metadata_api_stag_super_0 -h db-mysql-512ce0a.azure-eastus.github.net -P 3306 -D trust_metadata_api_staging -p
```

4. Run a migration with

```shell
migrate -source file://db/migrations -database 'mysql://trust_metadata_api_stag_super_0:<PASSWORD>@tcp(db-mysql-512ce0a.azure-eastus.github.net:3306)/trust_metadata_api_staging?multiStatements=true' up
```

> If you receive an error dialing TCP, it could be related to this Go DNS issue [https://github.com/golang/go/issues/12524](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/12524). To get around this, use the IP address instead of the host name in the migration command. To get the IP address, ping the hostname: `ping db-mysql-512ce0a.azure-eastus.github.net`

5. Check that the service still works as expected after the migration buy curling the service. For example: `curl -v https://trust-metadata-api-staging.githubapp.com/status`

## Production - Making Schema Changes on the DB Cluster

For running migrations on the production database cluster, see the [Database Migrations in Production with Skeema](./playbooks/database-migrations-prod-skeema.md) playbook.

## Working with Go and DB Queries

The Go interface to query the MySQL database is managed by [sqlc](https://sqlc.dev/).

To create additional queries:

- Add your query to `db/query/query.sql` alongside the existing queries or
  add it to a a new `.sql` file in that directory.
- Reference the [sqlc How To docs](https://docs.sqlc.dev/en/latest/index.html) for building different types of queries.
- Run `make dev-sqlc` to generate the `sqlc` files.

**DO NOT** manually edit any files in the `db/sqlc` directory. These are managed by the `sqlc` tool and are autogenerated.
